items.title: Actor Michael Wright, Star of ‘The Five Heartbeats’ and ‘V,’ Dies at 70
items.summary:
Michael Wright, the actor who played troubled lead singer Eddie King Jr. in Robert Townsend's 1991 musical drama "The Five Heartbeats," has died at 70. His wife, Susan Wright, announced the death in an Instagram post on Friday evening.

Wright died in Los Angeles on Wednesday, Aug. 19, after heart failure compounded by complications of Marchiafava-Bignami, a degenerative neurological disease, according to a family statement provided to TMZ and reported by Variety. He was born in New York City on April 30, 1956.

Over a career spanning more than 50 films and television shows, Wright appeared in "Streamers," "The Wanderers," "The Principal" and "Sugar Hill," and on the 1980s science-fiction series "V" and HBO's prison drama "Oz." His role in "The Five Heartbeats" — a fictional Motown-style group whose lead vocalist is pushed out by alcohol and drug addiction — remained the one audiences returned to most often.

"Michael was a husband, a father, a grandfather, loved one, a friend, and an extraordinary artist whose work touched generations," Susan Wright wrote, naming children Manon Wright, Byron Barr, Brittney Briggs, Brianna Barr and Sir Barr, and grandchild Yoko. "His talent, presence, and contributions to film and television will live on, but to those of us who loved him personally, he was so much more than the roles the world knew him for."

In a 2021 interview with Sheen Magazine, Wright described his approach to the work plainly: "The greatest sin an actor can commit is to fail to be interesting. I always try to make my characters interesting. I want you to be riveted and wonder what's going on behind my eyes." He also said he had no regrets, citing the places he had been and the five languages he spoke.

The family said it is grieving privately for now and will release further details about how it intends to honor Wright in the coming days.

items.title: Olivia Rodrigo Releases ‘Handmaid’s Tale’-Inspired Song, ‘Serena Joy,’ in a Tiny Run of CDs, With Digital Drop to Follow
items.summary:
Olivia Rodrigo released a new non-album song called "Serena Joy" on Friday, and for three days the only way to own it legally was to drive to Tustin, California. The track came out as a limited CD single, 500 copies pressed, sold exclusively at Analog Music Shop. The store said Friday night that all 500 had gone.

The title refers to the character in Margaret Atwood's "The Handmaid's Tale" who helps build a repressive patriarchy and then finds herself trapped inside it. The lyrics, printed on the front of the CD sleeve, never name the character, but the refrain does the work: "If they do it to them / They'll do it to you." An early verse runs, "Yeah, it's all for the cause / For the good of us all / And if you close your eyes / Then it can't be your fault."

Analog Music Shop, which has been the main source of official information about the release, said Rodrigo plans to send the song out digitally on Monday, and framed the arrangement as a gesture toward her all-female festival Daisy Chain Fields, happening next Saturday in nearby Irvine. "An artist building a stage for women in music and raising funds for women and girls," the shop wrote. "An artist willing to support a local independent record store."

Fans had known the song existed since June, when a studio photo listing 18 tracks under consideration for "You Look Pretty Sad for a Girl So in Love" surfaced online. Asked about it by Etalk two months ago, Rodrigo said, "I actually really love ['Serena Joy']. It didn't fit on the album. The record was very much a chronicle of a relationship — beginning, middle and end. But I hope that it'll be a part of something else down the line."

Variety reported that the audio leaked almost immediately despite the physical-only window, prompting takedown notices. Reaction online largely welcomed Rodrigo pushing past the breakup-record frame — one commenter on the song's Genius page wrote, "Forget hot girl summer — we're entering our dystopian propaganda era."

The digital release arrives Monday, six days before Daisy Chain Fields opens in Orange County.

items.title: Gavin Newsom Says Paramount Settlement Talks Happening in “Real Time,” Signals He’d Like a Deal
items.summary:
California Gov. Gavin Newsom said Friday that talks aimed at settling the antitrust suit against the Paramount-Warner Bros. merger are already underway, and made clear he would prefer a negotiated outcome to a trial. Speaking at a press appearance in San Francisco, he pointed to comments state Attorney General Rob Bonta made earlier in the week.

"Look, I was appreciative, I think this week, earlier this week, you heard the attorney general himself say he'd prefer this settled in the boardroom, not the courtroom," Newsom said. "So I think there's some universal sentiment there, if that's possible. The question is if that's possible. And what's the best deal, what's the landing?" He described the process as "unfolding, I assure you, in real time," with many meetings taking place, while noting that Bonta is one of a dozen state attorneys general in the coalition challenging the deal.

The remarks are the first time Newsom has addressed his position publicly. As The Hollywood Reporter noted, The Wall Street Journal reported on July 31 that the governor was worried about the suit's effect on California employment and had urged Bonta toward an out-of-court resolution; Newsom declined to confirm that account at the time.

He also responded to Paramount Skydance CEO David Ellison's threat to move one or two of Hollywood's remaining historic studios out of California if the case isn't resolved by October. "We're hoping that doesn't happen. And I'm of the belief that they don't want to see that happen," Newsom said. "It's not, I don't think, in the company's long-term interest, but I take it seriously."

Newsom said he has been speaking with people across the debate. "I'm very mindful of what this means to the state, I'm concerned about the state, our reputation," he said.

His position now matches that of Xavier Becerra, the Democratic candidate in this year's gubernatorial race, and Los Angeles Mayor Karen Bass, who called Thursday for both sides to come to the table and find common ground urgently. Twelve states remain plaintiffs in the suit.

items.title: Paramount Accuses Mark Ruffalo Of Being “Antisemitic” After He Slams Ellisons’ Ties To Oracle, Calling Them “Really Profoundly Scary People”
items.summary:
Paramount accused Mark Ruffalo of invoking "antisemitic tropes" after the actor attacked Larry and David Ellison's ties to Oracle in a series of Instagram Story posts opposing the Paramount-Warner Bros. merger. The exchange, reported by Deadline, marks the sharpest escalation yet in a public fight over a deal that 12 state attorneys general are suing to block.

Ruffalo shared a video of Oracle executive vice chair Safra Catz describing technology the company made available to the Israeli military. "This is the company that Larry Ellison is using to fund his son David's Warner Bros acquisition," he wrote, adding that the technologies "will most likely be merged into one of the largest media conglomerates in the world and one day used on you." He called the Ellisons "really profoundly scary people" and described Larry Ellison as "a classic Oligarch."

Much of Ruffalo's argument rested on jobs and market structure. He cited a projected loss of 4,500 direct filmmaking positions and roughly 10,000 ancillary jobs, argued the merger would raise cable prices and reduce competition, and called it "a classic antitrust case."

Paramount's response did not engage the antitrust claims. "We are, as always, troubled when antisemitic tropes are invoked in purported service of a business dispute," a spokesperson said, arguing that words like genocide and apartheid "aren't just wrong — they're a bridge too far, and they cheapen the very real suffering those words are meant to describe." The statement said the company wanted "less rhetoric, more understanding" and pledged "no blacklists, no exceptions, for anyone."

Ruffalo has been organizing against the deal for months. In April he joined attorney Norm Eisen in pressing state officials to intervene, gathering more than 5,000 signatures on an open letter — backed by the Committee for the First Amendment, the Future Film Coalition, the Writers Guild of America and the Democracy Defenders Fund — warning the takeover would threaten the sustainability of the creative community.

The dispute follows Netflix's February decision to abandon its own pursuit of Warner Bros. rather than top Paramount Skydance's $31-per-share offer, after signing an $82.7 billion deal with WBD in December. Los Angeles Mayor Karen Bass called Thursday for all parties to come to the table and move the merger forward.

items.title: Bonnaroo Taking “A Much-Needed Year Off” In 2027
items.summary:
Bonnaroo will not take place in 2027. Organizers announced Friday that the Manchester, Tennessee festival is taking what they called "a much-needed year off," with plans to return in 2028.

The reason is the ground itself. In a statement posted to the festival's social accounts and reported by Stereogum, the Bonnaroo team said it spent heavily ahead of the 2026 edition on improved drainage, 4.5 miles of new roadway and 135 acres of new grass — but that consecutive years of storms, including a heavy rainstorm this past Sunday, have left the Farm, and the main venue in particular, in need of recovery time.

The weather record backs it up. Bonnaroo scrapped its 2020 event because of COVID, canceled in 2021 due to flooding, and lost most of the 2025 weekend to severe weather, which prompted organizers to survey attendees about moving the festival to a different part of the calendar. The fest kept its usual mid-June slot in 2026 anyway, and storms wiped out 11 Sunday sets, including Aly & AJ for the second consecutive year.

Bonnaroo has run on the Farm since 2002. "This wasn't an easy decision, and not one we take lightly, but in our hearts, we know this break will only make Bonnaroo better," the statement read, thanking attendees for "an epic Bonnaroo 2026."

Organizers gave no date or lineup details for the 2028 return, and did not indicate whether the June weekend will hold when the festival comes back.
